cases.name: an-anomaly-share-that-is-not-a-number
cases.description: Both probabilities were parsed only where they are used, so check called this valid and the run then refused it. A check that passes what the next command rejects teaches the reader to distrust it.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="3" seed="s" local="en"><sequence name="X"><gen type="text" value="a,b,c" anomaly="10x"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>${{X}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: an-anomaly-share-above-one
cases.description: A share of values, so 2 is not a bigger request than 1 — it is not a share at all.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="3" seed="s" local="en"><sequence name="X"><gen type="number" value="1..9" anomaly="2"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>${{X}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: a-missing-share-above-one
cases.description: The same range, on the other imperfection wrapper — one code covers both because it is one mistake.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="3" seed="s" local="en"><sequence name="X"><gen type="number" value="1..9" missing="2"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>${{X}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: an-anomaly-on-a-list-with-no-numbers-in-it
cases.description: An anomaly multiplies a numeric value, so a list of words comes back unchanged: the config asks for 30% outliers, gets none, and nothing is said. Refused rather than warned, for the same reason anomaly_flag with no anomaly is refused — there is nothing to act on.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="3" seed="s" local="en"><sequence name="X"><gen type="text" value="alpha,beta,gamma" anomaly="0.3"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>${{X}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: an-anomaly-on-a-list-that-holds-one-number
cases.description: One number in the list is enough to perturb, so this is left alone. The half of the check that must never fire: only a list with nothing numeric anywhere in it is refused.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="3" seed="s" local="en"><sequence name="X"><gen type="text" value="alpha,42,gamma" anomaly="0.3"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>${{X}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: anomaly-flag-inside-case
cases.description: anomaly_flag on a <gen> inside a <case>. A case body is a concatenation, so a flag on one part does not describe the row; <mix flag="NAME"> is where the question has an answer. It used to be accepted and do nothing, and the only sign was ${{Out}} reaching the data as literal characters.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="2" seed="s"><sequence name="K"><gen type="text" value="a,b"/></sequence><switch name="S" on="K"><case is="a"><gen type="number" value="1..9" anomaly="0.5" anomaly_flag="Out"/></case><default><data>x</data></default></switch></env><block><line><data>${{S}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: anomaly-flag-on-a-compound-field
cases.description: The same shape one level out: a sequence mints the ground-truth column only where the flagged gen IS the sequence's value. Give the body a second part — another gen, a <data> literal, or a name= that makes this gen a field — and nothing was minted, while the anomaly still fired and ${{F}} reached the output as literal characters.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="4" seed="s" local="en"><sequence name="Rec"><gen type="text" value="n="/><gen type="number" value="10..99" name="amt" anomaly="0.5" anomaly_flag="F"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>${{Rec}} f=${{F}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: anomaly-flag-on-a-sequence-of-its-own
cases.description: The other side of the same boundary: one gen, one sequence, one flag column — this is what the refusal points the reader at, so it must stay valid.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="4" seed="s" local="en"><sequence name="Amount"><gen type="number" value="10..99" anomaly="0.5" anomaly_flag="F"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>${{Amount}} f=${{F}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: missing-when-with-no-rate
cases.description: A condition and no rate decides nothing — the config reads as if it did something and does not.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="3" seed="s" local="en"><sequence name="Age"><gen type="number" value="18..60"/></sequence><sequence name="X"><gen type="text" value="a,b,c" missing_when="Age < 30"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>${{X}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: missing-when-left-empty
cases.description: An empty condition is not "every row" — dropping the attribute says that. Written and blank, it is a question nobody finished asking.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="3" seed="s" local="en"><sequence name="X"><gen type="text" value="a,b,c" missing="0.4" missing_when=""/></sequence></env><block><line><data>${{X}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: missing-when-names-no-column
cases.description: A misspelled column is a legal bare word here, so the condition would simply never fire and blank nothing, silently. Reported by the same pass that reports it for if=.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="3" seed="s" local="en"><sequence name="Age"><gen type="number" value="18..60"/></sequence><sequence name="X"><gen type="text" value="a,b,c" missing="0.4" missing_when="Agee < 30"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>${{X}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: missing-when-on-a-repeated-cell
cases.description: A repeated cell holds several values on one row and the condition asks about one. Both readings are defensible — test each element, or test the row — so the combination is refused rather than guessed at. It was accepted and ignored: every element was blanked at the plain rate, from a config check had called valid.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="3" seed="s" local="en"><sequence name="X"><gen type="number" value="1..99" repeat="2" missing="0.4" missing_when="_value > 50"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>${{X}}</data></line></block></tdc>
